body:
I can reproduce the issue and the problem is in 
https://github.com/nunit/nunit/blob/6d030213f861161f25badb3a5a6ac147c9dc1e95/src/NUnitFramework/framework/Internal/TypeHelper.cs#L244-L258
where we change the integer into a float.

I don't know much about this area of the codebase, and it looks like this behaviour is old. It was introduced in https://github.com/nunit/nunit/commit/57f64ef3a3b0c52a73df09512687d11c421d60a9#diff-f6d1cef53e8881b5735640354e2d8f5d with the commit message "convert args in advance to support building for the compact framework", so perhaps it is no longer necessary, but this will require a more thorough examination.

I vaguely recall that we needed to do this for CF. The conversion was handled automatically for other platforms. That may or may not still be true but as it's tested it should be easy to see.

My suspicion is that the conversion may be done once and cached rather than for each method, but I haven't had time to check - we have a visitor for the holidays.

I tried to remove `TypeHelper.ConvertArgumentList` (the method called above) and that solved the problem, and all the other tests were still executed successfully.

The only "problem" I have with removing `TypeHelper.ConvertArgumentList` is that it is public - although in the `NUnit.Framework.Internal` namespace. I tried to search for other usages of this method in other projects on the internet, but I did not find any. The only results I got was this codebase and the issue #1881.

Personally, I think we should remove the usage and the method, but we can also remove the usage and obsolete the method (and the remove the method in a later release).

issue.title: [WIP] Remove TypeHelper.ConvertArgumentList
issue.body:
The added tests failed with the message "Object of type 'System.Single'
cannot be converted to type 'System.Int32'. The removal of
`TypeHelper.ConvertArgumentList` solves the problem.

Fixes #3125

body:
I've created a PR, but I would like for somebody else than Chris to review to ensure that we have consensus about removing `TypeHelper.ConvertArgumentList`.

EDIT: Apparently, the behaviour is different on Mono, so the change makes the code fail (I wonder if it still fails with `TypeHelper.ConvertArgumentList` in the codebase?).

This code has never had a CF conditional around it, so it was not added specifically for CF.

Perhaps it does affect other platforms as well?

I will try taking it out and see if it breaks CF.  Will report back after new years.

I'm pretty sure that's why I added it... which is why I wrote the comment. Strictly speaking, it could have been a limitation of the C# implementation in VS2008, which we used to compile that version, rather than CF itself.

Originally, NUnit only verified that the type was convertible but allowed .NET to make the conversion when invoking the test method. My recollection is that this did not work in some version of CF and I added a pre-conversion step. So long as the code worked under all platforms, I would not normally have put it in conditionally. My general outlook is to minimize the number of conditionals where possible so that the same code is always exercised. This maximizes the chance that a bug will be caught.

Also... I would say if it works now without the code, remove it. But if it is needed on any platform, leave it in. If you leave it in, the bug can be fixed by moving the code to where it will be called for each use of the data source rather than just once.

Since it will be very difficult to test this exhaustively, I would suggest doing what @CharliePoole suggests:  move the code to where it will be called for each use of the data source rather then just once.

issue.title: Consolidate type conversion code
issue.body:
There's currently a few places in the codebase that NUnit converts types for the purpose of input/output to tests. The ones I've noticed are:
- https://github.com/nunit/nunit/blob/9a98666/src/NUnitFramework/framework/Internal/TypeHelper.cs#L230
- https://github.com/nunit/nunit/blob/df130ce/src/NUnitFramework/framework/Attributes/TestCaseAttribute.cs#L395
- https://github.com/nunit/nunit/blob/3a8ee04/src/NUnitFramework/framework/Internal/ParamAttributeTypeConversions.cs#L91
- https://github.com/nunit/nunit/blob/061f435/src/NUnitFramework/framework/Internal/Reflect.cs#L223

Over time, some of these have drifted out of sync with each other (for example, present master has a `TestCaseAttribute` which will implicitly convert `int` -> `long`, but a `RangeAttribute` which does not).

Most of these conversion functions all focus on the `IConvertible` types, and mimic a subset of C#'s implicitly convertible types. Based on recollection from @CharliePoole this was likely added for CompactFramework, and "may" no longer be necessary. https://github.com/nunit/nunit/issues/3125#issuecomment-450432111

At present there's 2 open PRs that incidentally consolidate + remove some of these functions in order to address other issues.
- https://github.com/nunit/nunit/pull/3098
- https://github.com/nunit/nunit/pull/3133

I think if we consolidate other usages, it would both simplify the codebase, as well as facilitate future change (or removal of the implicit C# conversion code, if that's a goal)

body:
There's been a few different functions that do type conversions for parameters that have slowly been consolidated into `ParamAttributeTypeConversions`:

https://github.com/nunit/nunit/blob/master/src/NUnitFramework/framework/Internal/ParamAttributeTypeConversions.cs#L101

It looks like that doesn't currently convert "single". Would a good first step for this be to add single support to that function, and then have TestCaseSource call it instead? I figure if the goal is to eventually remove pre-conversions, it might be easiest to do if they're all in one place

The original goal was for each attribute to be independent, allowing for user-defined attributes to work as the creator might see fit.

Not sure what the current goal is as it's not articulated.
Oh I see thanks for clarifying @CharliePoole  Then yes, consolidating type conversions may not be in line with that goal. I wasn't aware of that goal, or if it's changed

Nor am I. As you say, there has been some consolidation, which might imply a change. I'd prefer the intent to be articulated, which is why I made the comment.

One approach that might make sense would be to centralize "normal" conversions like int to double while separating in each attribute the "special" ones, like those from string.

issue.title: Drop pre-conversion of test case/fixture params where .NET supports it implicitly
issue.body:
NUnit has historically handled and pre-converted some type conversions when passing parameters to test cases/fixtures. These include both native-supported implicit conversions of primitives as per the ECMA spec (ex: `int` -> `long` or `short` -> `int`) and some special case conversions for ease-of-use (like `string` -> `DateTime`). Preconversion of primitives within NUnit of types also implicitly converted by netfx + netcore has also meant some bugs and added complexity:
- https://github.com/nunit/nunit/issues/3125
- https://github.com/nunit/nunit/issues/2638
- https://github.com/nunit/nunit/issues/3219

I think it should be considered to drop this preconversion of NUnit-provided ECMA-defined implicit conversions. This would _not_ include removing ease-of-use custom conversions like `string` -> `DateTime` which _should_ make it a relatively transparent change to consumers. One point of discussion is that this preconversion was originally added for Compact Framework, and that removing it could disrupt any CF consumers (if that is still supported)

I'd like to hear some thoughts on this.
